description: Added an explicit rule that distress reactions (crying, getting upset, almost vomiting, feeling sick, shaking) are NOT a behavior type and must not be classified as safety/avoidance/escape or split into a separate behavior; instead attach the distress detail to the accompanying behavior's description or omit it. This addresses repeated over-classification where distress was turned into an extra behavior or a spurious 'safety' entry (cases 3, 5, 10, 11, 12).
Strengthened the 'do not label safety unless reassurance/protection sought' rule to explicitly include a child being upset or explaining why as not constituting a safety behavior.
Clarified in the split-notes rule that a distress reaction must not be split off from the behavior it accompanies.

Added a rule prohibiting editorial or meta commentary as a behavior entry (e.g. 'Hard to tell whether these behaviors continued'), directing use of a single 'unclear' behavior only for genuine ambiguity (case 15).
Added a 'Faithfulness to the note' section requiring preservation of original speaker and pronouns in quotes/paraphrases (case 15 pronoun shift).

Added guidance to capture brief/passive accommodations such as encouraging the child to try again next time, and added a matching accommodation example and updated the passive-accommodation rule (case 2 missing accommodation).
Added a worked example showing distress accompanying a refusal counted as a single avoidance behavior plus separate accommodations, to reinforce the new distress rule.
Bumped draft version note from v2 to v3.
